question: In India, electronic records (including electronic medical records) can be admitted as evidence in court without a Section 65B certificate under the Indian Evidence Act, provided the original electronic device is available.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. Under Indian law, a Section 65B certificate (now Section 63, BSA 2023) is mandatory for the admission of electronic records as secondary evidence, and courts have held it is required even when the original device is produced. Failure to attach this certificate is the most common reason electronic medical records are challenged or excluded in medicolegal proceedings.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act (now Section 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023) requires a certificate from a responsible person for any electronic record tendered as evidence, regardless of whether the original device is available. Omitting the certificate is fatal to admissibility.
